purpose: Source-only manual coverage checklist frozen before reading the generated graph. Diagnostic review, not an independent benchmark or question-derived gold set.

source.title: Amazon sellers sound off on the FTC's 'long-overdue' antitrust case

review_rules: Derived only from this supplied article record; no questions, answers, evidence labels or generated graph were consulted.
Count distinct supported meanings, not edge quantity. A qualified fact may satisfy several rows; a combined row requires all stated participants, values and qualifications.

Graph-fact coverage requires addressable participants joined to the asserted predicate, value and conditions. Finding the wording only through the retained article counts as source-access coverage separately.
Preserve reported observations, allegations, opinions, predictions and uncertainty as distinct meanings with source attribution; retention does not independently establish truth.
Keep source dates, relative dates, currency notation and approximation as given. Do not repair conflicting chronology or fill omitted fields from outside knowledge.
Publication metadata, navigation and collection artifacts are audited separately and must not inflate domain-assertion coverage.

editorial_and_publication_meanings.meaning: CNBC is the supplied publisher label and the author field is null. Preserve the exact title, URL, business category and 2023-10-06 publication timestamp without inventing an author.
CNBC says it viewed the Amazon eligibility email to Ruckel; keep this evidential basis distinct from anonymous forum comments and FTC allegations.

The article says Nearly three years later after an October 27, 2021 incident, despite the supplied October 2023 publication date. Retain this source inconsistency without revising dates or deriving a three-year interval as verified.

The opening photo caption shows a worker sorting parcels at the outbound dock of Amazon's Eastvale, California fulfillment center on August 31, 2021. It is image context, not the date or location of the seller incidents.
The source states that antitrust remedies are often decided after a liability finding. This is explanatory background, not a case-specific ruling or an independently verified legal rule.

Photo credits identify the opening photograph source, a Fred Ruckel credit for the Snuggly Cat/Ripple Rug image, and a courtesy Molson Hart caption. They do not identify the article author or establish independent corroboration of every claim.
watch now is an embedded-media/navigation label. No video transcript or additional video evidence is supplied; the final Hart passage has no reported incident resolution.

section_coverage.meaning: Section labels organize this source; they are not independent domain facts or taxonomic is-a links.

negative_checks: Keep Ruckel/Snuggly Cat/Ripple Rug/Chewy/October 2021 separate from Hart/Viahart/Brain Flakes/Target/September 2022.
Do not equate buy-box loss with deletion of the product listing or assert verified realized daily losses without a supplied amount.
Do not compare Chewy's $39.99 item price with its $48.54 delivered total as if they were the same measure; preserve the $43 Amazon comparison.
Ruckel chose to ask Chewy for a price increase; no actual price increase, restored eligibility or final resolution is supplied.
Do not repair the Nearly three years later chronology or substitute publication time for incident time.
FTC allegations, Amazon defenses and individual seller experiences must remain attributed and may conflict; none alone is an adjudicated finding.
No specific court remedy, completed liability judgment, universal FBA requirement or guaranteed two-day delivery may be invented.
Keep Moller's $7.49-versus-about-$12 costs tied to his own shipping example and do not treat them as marketplace-wide tariffs.
Do not give anonymous commenters invented identities, universal seller consensus or literal gambling/drug/debt facts from their metaphors.
Keep Needham's seller/service-provider roles, Moller's brand/unnamed agency, and Hart's company distinct.
Do not convert about 90 percent of Hart's business into a precise audited revenue or profit share.
Do not fill the unreported outcome or numerical prices of Hart's Target incident from another seller's story.
Generic related-to edges or prose-only summaries do not satisfy the person-company-product-platform, allegation-speaker-policy, price-basis and comparison joins.
